Tenant.title: Tenant
Tenant.description: Represents a single business or store within the FreshTally application, acting as a container for all operational data.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Tenant entity.

name.description: The official name of the business or store.

address.description: The physical address of the business.

contactEmail.description: The primary contact email for the tenant.

phoneNumber.description: The primary contact phone number for the tenant.

currency.description: The default currency used for transactions, e.g., 'USD', 'EUR'.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the tenant record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the tenant record was last updated.

UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user associated with a specific tenant, defining their access and identity within the application. Authentication details are managed externally.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. Corresponds to the authentication system's user ID.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant this user belongs to. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N UserProfile)

role.description: The role of the user within the tenant (e.g., 'owner', 'staff').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents an item or service that a tenant sells, including inventory and pricing details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant that owns this product. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N Product)

name.description: The name of the product or service.

description.description: A detailed description of the product or service.

price.description: The current selling price of the product.

costPrice.description: The cost of the product to the business for inventory management.

stockLevel.description: The current quantity of the product available in inventory.

sku.description: Stock Keeping Unit, a unique identifier for the product often used for scanning.

barcode.description: The barcode value for the product, if applicable.

imageUrl.description: URL to an image of the product.

isActive.description: Indicates if the product is currently active and available for sale.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the product was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the product was last updated.

Transaction.title: Transaction
Transaction.description: Records a complete sales transaction, including total amounts, payment methods, and responsible staff.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Transaction entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant where this transaction occurred. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N Transaction)

transactionDate.description: The date and time when the transaction was completed.

totalAmount.description: The total monetary amount of the transaction.

paymentMethod.description: The method of payment used (e.g., 'Cash', 'Credit Card', 'Mobile Pay').

staffId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who processed this transaction. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Transaction)

status.description: The current status of the transaction (e.g., 'completed', 'pending', 'refunded', 'voided').

notes.description: Any additional notes about the transaction.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the transaction record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the transaction record was last updated.

TransactionItem.title: TransactionItem
TransactionItem.description: Details a specific product included within a transaction, capturing its quantity and price at the time of sale.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TransactionItem entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant where this transaction item belongs. (Inherited from Transaction for multi-tenancy context)

transactionId.description: Reference to the Transaction this item is part of. (Relationship: Transaction 1:N TransactionItem)

productId.description: Reference to the Product sold in this transaction item. (Relationship: Product 1:N TransactionItem)

quantity.description: The quantity of the product sold in this transaction item.

unitPrice.description: The unit price of the product at the time of sale.

subtotal.description: The subtotal for this transaction item (quantity * unitPrice).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the transaction item was created.

Expense.title: Expense
Expense.description: Records a business expense incurred by a tenant, including its amount, date, and AI-categorized classification.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Expense entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant that incurred this expense. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N Expense)

description.description: A brief description of the expense.

amount.description: The monetary amount of the expense.

expenseDate.description: The date when the expense was incurred.

category.description: The categorization of the expense (e.g., 'Utilities', 'Rent', 'Supplies', 'Marketing'). This can be AI-powered or manually assigned.

notes.description: Any additional notes or details about the expense.

receiptUrl.description: URL to the scanned or digital receipt for the expense.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the expense record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the expense record was last updated.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure is designed to strictly enforce multi-tenancy and role-based access control, adhering to the core design principles, especially Authorization Independence and QAP compliance. The central strategy is to use a top-level `userProfiles` collection as the single source of truth for a user's current tenant association and role, and then nest all tenant-specific data under a `/tenants/{tenantId}` path.

**Authorization Independence:** This is primarily achieved by:
1.  **`userProfiles/{userId}` Collection:** Each authenticated user (`request.auth.uid`) will have a corresponding document in `/userProfiles/{userId}`. This document explicitly stores the `tenantId` that the user belongs to, along with their `role` (e.g., 'owner', 'staff'). Firestore Security Rules can efficiently `get()` this `userProfile` document using `request.auth.uid` to determine the user's `tenantId` and `role` without relying on `get()` calls to parent *data* documents in the `/tenants` hierarchy. This approach ensures atomic creation of tenant-specific data and simplifies rule debugging.
2.  **Denormalized `tenantId`:** Every document within the `/tenants/{tenantId}` subcollections (Products, Transactions, Expenses, TransactionItems) will explicitly include a `tenantId` field. While the primary authorization check for `list` operations will leverage the path's `tenantId` against the user's `userProfile.tenantId`, this denormalized field provides an additional integrity check and simplifies single-document `get` access where the path might not explicitly expose `tenantId` if the document were moved.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** This structure directly addresses the reported permissions error on `list` operations for `/tenants/72751/transactions` by ensuring QAP compliance:
1.  **Path-Based Scoping:** All tenant-specific data is rooted under `/tenants/{tenantId}/...`. When a user attempts a `list` operation on a collection like `/tenants/{tenantId}/transactions`, the `{tenantId}` wildcard in the path *must* match the `tenantId` stored in the user's `userProfile` document (`get(/userProfiles/$(request.auth.uid)).data.tenantId`).
2.  **Explicit Authorization Check:** The security rules will perform a direct lookup: `allow list: if get(/userProfiles/$(request.auth.uid)).data.tenantId == tenantId && ... (role-based permissions)`. This ensures that every document potentially returned by a `list` query *must* belong to the `tenantId` specified in the path, and that the authenticated user is a legitimate member of that specific tenant. This prevents data leakage and ensures that `list` queries are inherently secure and not filtered after the fact, resolving the common permissions error for `list` operations.

**Structural Segregation and Access Modeling:**
*   **`userProfiles`:** Dedicated for user-specific data, accessible only by the user themselves. Its primary purpose is authorization lookup.
*   **`tenants`:** Contains top-level tenant information. Access is controlled by checking the user's `userProfile`.
*   **Nested Collections:** `products`, `transactions`, `expenses` are subcollections of `tenants/{tenantId}`. `items` are nested under `transactions/{transactionId}`. This hierarchical structure with explicit `tenantId` parameters in the path ensures strict data isolation between tenants.
*   **DBAC:** User roles (owner/staff) are stored within the `UserProfile` document and are used directly in security rules to grant granular permissions (e.g., 'owner' can `delete`, 'staff' can only `read` and `create`).

This robust design ensures that a user's identity and permissions are consistently checked at the entry point of any tenant-specific data access, simplifying security rules and enhancing debuggability.
